newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Duma seen considering budget cuts May 21.
newsitem.headline: Russian Duma seen considering budget cuts May 21.

text.p: Russia's lower house of parliament will probably consider budget cuts on May 21 but is unlikely to pass huge government-recommended changes, the speaker of the State Duma said on Tuesday.

"I think that today or tomorrow we will get it and will be able to put it (on the agenda for) May 21, meeting all the necessary requirements," Gennady Seleznyov, a member of the Communist Party, said of the bill on cutting the budget.
Under the 1997 budget law, if revenues in any quarter are less than 90 percent of what is planned, the government must present a bill to the Duma sequestering, or cutting, spending.

Revenues in the first quarter were only 60 percent of budgeted levels. The government now acknowledges there is not enough money to fulfil the budget passed by parliament but the Duma is hesitant to agree to all the cuts.
The government, due to consider the cuts at Wednesday's weekly cabinet meeting, will present its calculations of budget fulfilment on May 21.

First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais has said 1997 revenues would be about 100 trillion roubles under target. The budget called for total revenues of 529.8 trillion roubles and revenues at 434 trillion roubles.
But Seleznyov said the Duma, which wrangled with the government on the 1997 budget for months, would not be likely to quickly pass huge cuts.
